payload.feature:
FIX ROUND 991b for issue #991: AFTER A REFUSAL'S WORDS ARE MASKED, NOTHING MAY REWRITE THEM BUT A PURE TRUNCATION, SO NO WHITESPACE COLLAPSE OR CUT CAN REBUILD A BOUND SECRET. UNDER-LIMIT WORDS CROSS THE BOUNDARY BYTE FOR BYTE.

The branch is story-991-masked-refusal-bound, checked out in this worktree at 1196a09bd (on main 9532a9d57). When you are done, the branch is 1196a09bd plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks.

WHERE IT STANDS:
- **Unit 991** (implement-issue-991-430-slice-4a-4008161f) re-bounded the masked words in `masked_refusal` (adapters.rs about :6262) with `bounded_wire_line` (adapters/refusal.rs:22). It stopped at a SECURITY HOLD.
- **HIGH (security), the chief's, reproduced:**
  - `bounded_wire_line` collapses runs of whitespace and control characters as well as cutting, so running it AFTER the mask can rebuild a bound secret.
  - **The case:** a Claude shim emits `{"type":"result","is_error":true,"error": "x" * 70 + "TOPSECRET y","apiErrorStatus":429}`, with `API_TOKEN` bound to the synthetic value `TOPSECRET (`, pinned `--model featherless:qwen/qwen3`.
  - The token's first cut ends in a space, so the pre-mask words contain `TOPSECRET  (HTTP 429)`: two spaces, and no complete secret. Masking therefore replaces nothing. The re-collapse then emits `TOPSECRET (`, the literal bound value, in readable words: 91 characters become 90.
  - It happens for an ordinary attempt and for a probe (`probe: true`), read back through `PreSessionRefusal::read`.
  - Adding a second binding whose name is 250 `Z` and whose value is `HTTP` makes the masked words 346 characters, and the cut to 300 STILL rebuilds `API_TOKEN`'s value.
- **LOW (correctness):** under the limit, the re-collapse also changes text. With 159 `x` + space + `y`, no secrets and status 429, the masked words should stay 183 characters, trailing space included; they become 182.
- The chief's six scratch tests (`chief_991_{under_limit_trailing_space,under_limit_post_mask_secret,over_limit_post_mask_secret}_{ordinary,probe}`) all failed at HEAD.

THE OPERATOR'S RULING: taken under the standing ruling of 2026-11-04 ("go with recommended on anything else that comes up", "and by hand"), recorded on #991 (https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/991#issuecomment-6630566719). This fix round, as follows.

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. **Only a pure truncation after the mask.**
   - In `masked_refusal`, replace the `bounded_wire_line` re-cut with a truncation to `REFUSAL_WORDS_LIMIT` characters at a char boundary (`chars().take(limit)`, or the house's char-boundary cut if one exists). Apply it only when the masked words exceed the limit.
   - Under-limit masked words are passed through unchanged, byte for byte.
   - Rewrite the comment to state the invariant: masking is the last REWRITE. A prefix of masked text holds no substring the whole lacks, so a truncation cannot rebuild a value. A collapse or any other rewrite after the mask could.
2. **Check the first collapse, which runs before masking.**
   - `bounded_wire_line` builds the excerpt from raw stream text, collapsing whitespace and control characters, and masking only runs afterwards.
   - **The question:** can a bound value containing whitespace or control characters (`"a\nb"`, `"a  b"`, a tab) reach the words in collapsed form (`"a b"`), which masking for the raw value then misses?
   - Write the test. If it leaks, fix it (recommended): mask each value's collapsed form too, in `masked_refusal` or `secret::mask_text`'s caller, so both forms are replaced.
   - If it cannot leak, the test shows it, and your notes say why.
3. **Tests:**
   - the chief's six cases, under your own names, each read back through `PreSessionRefusal::read`. Each asserts that the words contain no bound value and that the class, provider, route and status are kept, and gives the exact words or their exact length:
     - under the limit with a trailing space, which stays 183 characters, byte for byte;
     - under the limit, a secret rebuilt by a collapse, which must not appear;
     - over the limit, a secret rebuilt by the cut, which must not appear, with the words exactly 300 characters;
     - each one for an ordinary attempt and for a probe.
   - step 2's case;
   - #991's original case (160 `x`, a 140-`X` name bound to `HTTP`) still reads back bounded to 300.

Removal controls (record each in the commit message, restored after the observed failure):
- (i) Put the `bounded_wire_line` re-cut back. The post-mask-secret tests must fail by name, showing the value.
- (ii) Apply the truncation to under-limit text through the old collapse. The trailing-space test must fail by name.
- (iii) If step 2 found a leak, drop the collapsed-form masking. Step 2's test must fail by name.

GATES:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked adapters:: (timeout 280; split by filter if it cannot finish)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check
- TMPDIR stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.
- A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call. A call that outlasts it leaves its command running and blocks the calls behind it, including the write of your result file. So:
  - wrap every command in `timeout 280` there;
  - if a gate still cannot finish inside the limit, report it UNVERIFIED (the controller's host coverage runs every test) rather than retrying it;
  - write your result file before any optional extra check.
- Commit when done, signed off (`git commit -s`), "protocol: …" ending "(#991)". Leave a blank line before the trailers. "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" comes LAST, directly after the sign-off. Record each removal control in the commit message. Never push.

ASKS TO NAME (for the PR, which opens as a DRAFT only if one is new):
- step 2's result, and its fix if it leaked;
- any new one. No public API change is expected.

SIZE (an estimate): production about ±10 lines; +80 to +180 test lines.

KNOWN FLAKES, not this branch's:
- capability_broker tests and `machine_proof::` runs failing "MCP server box filesystem identity is not protected" under host load;
- brokkr-runtime engine::broker admission tests ending `Identity(Expired)` under load;
- heap_costs' one-byte compare difference under load.

If verify fails on one of these alone, the implement visit reruns it on the host alone (`-- --exact`, with HOME set), quotes both results, makes no commit, and reports COMPLETE, not blocked.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-9d or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- **This unit holds the ONE adapters.rs slot.**
- **#966** (another lane) edits only brokkr-protocol's process/tests.rs.
- **430s4bL3** (another lane) owns crates/brokkr-runtime/src/admission/host*.
- **753s4m2** (another lane) is in brokkr-core and brokkr-store's event_index*.
- **9d's units** own #317 (decision 0064), the CI scripts and witnesses.json.
- This unit edits adapters.rs's `masked_refusal`, the secret masking's caller if step 2 needs it, and their tests. Leave everything else.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit. For a scratch, use `git worktree add` or `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into /var/tmp, never a byte copy of this worktree. It reports each finding as a test case: the shim stream and bound secrets set up, the call made, and the refusal words observed against the ones expected.

Decisions: 0012 (secrets masked at the driver boundary, layer 5); 0103 (accepted; ruling 1(a), the bounded words); 0071 rulings 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9; 0063 (Linux and macOS). 2026-09-26, the threat model: fail closed on what cannot be read.

YOUR SEAT: you run on dsh (DeepSeek Flash, DeepSeek's platform), unboxed with dsh's own tools, at the operator's word (2026-10-26). Sign off every commit (`git commit -s`).

a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Implemented FIX ROUND 991b. In crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs `masked_refusal`, the post-mask `bounded_wire_line` re-cut is replaced by a pure char-boundary truncation to REFUSAL_WORDS_LIMIT, applied only when the masked words exceed it; under-limit words now cross byte for byte (trailing space kept) and the comment states that masking is the last rewrite. Step 2 found no leak: every harness event is `mask_json`-masked on its decoded strings at the stream edge before `refusal_reason` calls `bounded_wire_line`, so a value holding whitespace or a control character is already replaced before it could reach the words in collapsed form. `masked_refusal_991b_does_not_leak_a_value_rewritten_by_the_first_collapse` proves that end to end, and it failed with `before a b and c de and e fg after` when the pre-classifier `secret::mask_json` was removed. No production change was needed for step 2. Tests: the chief's six cases (under-limit trailing space = 183 chars byte for byte; under-limit post-mask secret stays 91 with `TOPSECRET  (` and no `TOPSECRET (`; over-limit post-mask secret is exactly 300 with no value) each on an ordinary attempt and a probe, every one through production `run_seat` and `PreSessionRefusal::read`, pinning class/provider/route/status; #991's original 160-x/140-X case still reads back bounded to 300. Removal controls observed then restored: (i) the old `bounded_wire_line` re-cut made all four post-mask-secret tests fail by name showing `TOPSECRET (`; (ii) the old collapse on under-limit text made both trailing-space tests fail by name (182 vs the required 183); (iii) not applicable because step 2 found no leak, so the step-2 test was bound against the pre-classifier mask instead. Gates: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked 'adapters::'` (541 passed), `typos --hidden`, `quality/ratchet.sh files|clones|api`, `git diff --check`, and `cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self` all exit 0. `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` hit the 280s seat limit with no failure observed (UNVERIFIED; host coverage runs every test); exact coverage remains pending the external host/CI run. `/var/tmp` was read-only in this sandbox, so `TMPDIR=/tmp` (outside the worktree) was used. No new ask; no public API change.

Verified against all three chief cases: the 183-char trailing-space line, the 91-char two-space line the old collapse rebuilt into the bound value 'TOPSECRET (', and the 346-to-300 over-limit cut; both call sites (ordinary 6500, probe 6479) pass the one choke point, and the reader's <=300-char filter (lib.rs:244) matches the cut exactly. STEP 2: NO LEAK. Every harness event is secret::mask_json-masked on its decoded strings (keys included) at the stream edge before any classifier collapse - verified at all four decode-then-classify sites (claude 2448, codex 3636, dsh 2313 and 4866) plus masked stderr (2480, 5316) and the result file (6682); the five other decode sites (thread settings 1713, transcript/journal headers 2218/3876/4087, engine protocol 6772) never feed refusal_reason. A bound value holding a run of whitespace or a control character is replaced in raw form before the first collapse, so its collapsed form never reaches the words; the new end-to-end test (DOUBLE_SPACE/TAB/CONTROL) pins this and passes at HEAD. No fix needed, no new ask. Control (iii) is recorded as not applicable with a binding substitute: the exact-words assertion on the collapsed forms provably fails without the stream-edge mask. All eight cases read back through crate::PreSessionRefusal::read and pin class, provider, route, status and exact words or length. GATES re-run clean on this box: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked adapters:: (541 passed); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones, api; git diff --check; recipes/self compiles. I also ran the full workspace suite to close the commit's recorded UNVERIFIED: every failure here is environmental, not the commit's - 169 capability_broker::* in brokkr-cli's it (the documented flake; they panic ReadOnlyFilesystem on /var/tmp, which this seat's sandbox mounts read-only) and 22-33 hands::tests box-identity failures (Err(Identity)/Unprotected(Interpreter), the same box subsystem this box refuses to nest) which I reproduced on the pre-commit tree 1196a09bd (33 there, flaky by load as documented); one process:: test flaked once under full-suite load in #966's lane's file and passes alone; brokkr-bridge/core/store/view/runtime libs, all heap_* targets and protocol's own adapters:: are green. Contention respected: only adapters.rs's masked_refusal and round430_tests.rs changed; process/tests.rs, runtime admission, core and store untouched. No new decision document needed - the operator's #991 ruling governs and the commit cites decisions 0012 and 0103 with the removal controls recorded. FINDINGS: none at any severity. No security residual; the change removes a secret-rebuild path.
